tips: Use a separate radio receiver to tune these over-the-air frequencies. This directory contains station information, not audio streams; source links need an internet connection.
Hand-crank describes a power method, not reception capability. Check the radio specification for AM, FM and NOAA Weather Radio / WX; an AM/FM-only receiver cannot tune NOAA weather broadcasts.
The seven NOAA WX frequencies are 162.400, 162.425, 162.450, 162.475, 162.500, 162.525 and 162.550 MHz. Channel numbers vary by receiver; match the frequency in your manual.
Test reception before an emergency. The nearest or strongest transmitter may not carry alerts for your county. Verify county coverage and program SAME location codes if your receiver supports them.
Keep the receiver powered and follow its battery, antenna and alert-test instructions. Hearing a weather broadcast does not prove that automatic alert functions are enabled.
These are frequency references, not live status reports. Transmitters, station schedules and reception can change or fail during power outages. Keep more than one way to receive warnings.

The WX list covers the 28 NWS transmitters located in Michigan, not every signal receivable in Michigan. Some border counties use an out-of-state transmitter; consult the NWS county or station search when online.
